newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Jardine Fleming dismisses McCowan over PNG inquiry.
newsitem.headline: Jardine Fleming dismisses McCowan over PNG inquiry.

text.p: Jardine Fleming said on Wednesday that senior executive Rupert McCowan had been dismissed in connection with the Papua New Guinea mercenaries case.

"Following the (internal) investigation, and in light of the proceedings of the inquiry, Jardine Fleming has now terminated, with effect from today, the employment of Mr. Rupert McCowan, an assistant director in Jardine Fleming's capital markets division," Jardine Fleming said in a statement.
Jardine Fleming is 50 percent owned by Jardine Matheson Holdings Ltd.
Jardine Fleming said it launched its own internal inquiry when reports of the company's involvement surfaced at a government probe in Port Moresby, capital of the South Pacific nation.
Sacked PNG army chief Brigadier-General Jerry Singirok told the inquiry in April that McCowan attented a meeting in London in September 1996 at which a US$36 million mercenary deal was discussed.
He also said McCowan acted as the financial adviser in the mercenary deal.
The mercenaries were hired by the PNG government headed by then Prime Minister Julius Chan to help quell secessionist rebels in Bougainville, the site of a valuable copper mine.
Chan has stepped aside while the PNG inquiry continues.

"Mr. McCowan did not inform Jardine Fleming senior management of all of his activities in relation to Papua New Guinea and we believe that he acted beyond the scope of his authority as an employee of Jardine Fleming," Miles Armstrong, head of corporate finance, said in the statement.
A lawyer representing Jardine Fleming handed in a written submission to the PNG public inquiry on Tuesday.
In the statement, Jardine Fleming said the submission outlined the background to its involvement with the PNG government during and following the flotation of Orogen Minerals last year.
Orogen is 51 percent owned by the PNG government.
